identity.name: Moghulistan
alt_names: Eastern Chagatai Khanate (khanate of the Moghuls)

land.text: the Moghul khanate after Esen Buqa II's death in 1462: 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Moghulistan row begins in 1463 with the western half only; the eastern half is Cliopatria's East Turkestan row (east-turkestan dossier) until 1469.

land.text: the Tarim Basin, the Yarkent Khanate of Sultan Said Khan

successors.note: The Moghulistan page: Said Khan 'conquered the western Tarim Basin from Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat in 1514' and formed the Yarkent Khanate; Cliopatria's Eastern Moghulistan row begins in 1519.

land.text: Turpan, 'the eastern division of Moghulistan', founded by Ahmad Alaq in 1487 and ruled by Mansur Khan from 1503

successors.note: No Cliopatria row and no dossier yet (suggested slug turpan-khanate, Turpan Khanate page: 1487 to 1570 or later).

capitals.name: Aksu
capitals.note: Yunus Khan page: 'Ruling from Aksu as Khan, Yunus Khan maintained good relations with the Timurids'; after Dost Muhammad's death 'Yunus seized Aksu'. The pages name no seat for 1463-1469 and the Moghulistan page lists Almaliq as the capital of the whole 1347-1462 khanate, so no dot is drawn before 1470.

capitals.name: Tashkent
capitals.note: 'In 1484, Yunus Khan ... take Tashkent'; 'Yunus Khan died in Taskhent in 1487' and 'He was succeeded in Tashkent by his eldest son', Mahmud Khan (Yunus Khan page).

capitals.name: Turpan
capitals.note: Turpan Khanate page: founded by Ahmad Alaq in 1487 'based in Turpan', the eastern division of Moghulistan; Mansur Khan reigned 1503-1543. Said Khan's court at Kashgar (from 1514) belongs to the Yarkent Khanate. The dot from 1492 is the researcher's reading of Cliopatria's Tarim-and-Turfan shape.

keyframe_review.note: 464,954 km2 for 1463-1467 (70.1-81.1E, 38.5-46.5N): the western half, Yunus Khan's. 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan' (Esen Buqa II page); Yunus's territory is not outlined on any page opened (the Yunus page has an Issyk-Kul fief and Kashgar/Yarkand invitations, undated). No area on the pages. (unverified: page budget)

302,142 km2 (west edge moves from 70.3E to 71.4E, 136,000 km2 lost; no page dates it). Valid for 1468-1469 only: 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' (Moghulistan page); from 1470 see moghulistan_1470. (unverified: page budget) [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1468..1469 from this entry's own 'Valid for 1468-1469 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the western Moghul khanate joined to the Tarim Basin and Turfan of the former East Turkestan, the khanate 'reunited' by Yunus Khan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1475 shape (1,382,780 km2) is the 1468 Moghulistan shape plus the 1468 East Turkestan shape (3 and 2 cells of difference), i.e. the reunion of the khanate; the Moghulistan page puts the reunion after Dost Muhammad's death in 1469 ('After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate'), the Yunus Khan page has Yunus seize Aksu after Dost died 'in 1468 or 1469'. The 1475 shape is carried back to 1470.
1,382,780 km2 for 1475-1481: Zhetysu and the Tarim Basin under Yunus Khan. The page gives no area; 'Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' after 1469.

1,383,470 km2. Valid for 1482-1483 only; Tashkent is added from 1484 (moghulistan_1484). Yunus Khan page: 'In 1484, Yunus Khan took advantage of one of the periodic conflicts' between Sultan Ahmad and Umar Shaikh Mirza II, which allowed him 'to take possession of Tashkent' (the Moghulistan page also says 'took Tashkent in 1482'). The shape's west edge (71.4E) stops short of Tashkent (69.3E). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1482..1483 from this entry's own 'Valid for 1482-1483 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1482 shape with Tashkent, taken by Yunus Khan in 1484 from the Timurids

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1484-1491: the 1482 shape plus Tashkent. Yunus took Tashkent in 1484 and 'died in Taskhent in 1487'; 'He was succeeded in Tashkent by his eldest son', Sultan Mahmud Khan (ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent 1487-1508, Moghulistan page), so Tashkent stays with the western Moghul line when Cliopatria splits the row in 1492.

1,080,691 km2 for 1492-1511: the Tarim Basin and Turfan, the same outline as East Turkestan 1463-1474. The western part (Zhetysu, 253,000 km2 by the gazetteer) is the Cliopatria row eastern-chagatai-khanate, the part Mahmud Khan held from Tashkent. Turpan Khanate page: Ahmad Alaq founded the khanate in 1487 'based in Turpan', 'ruled the northern part of the Tarim Basin from Turpan'; Mansur 1503-1543. Yunus Khan page: 'the Moghuls in the east followed Ahmad Alaq'. The Dughlat Mirza Abu Bakr held Kashgar, Yarkand and Khotan in the same years (undated).

1,365,231 km2. Valid for 1512-1513 only; the shape is the 1511 Moghulistan shape joined again to the Zhetysu of eastern-chagatai-khanate (1 and 3 cells of difference), although the Moghulistan page says the Kyrgyz 'gained ground in the Tian Shan' and 'by 1510-11, they had effectively driven out the Moghuls'; kept at Cliopatria's outline, conflict noted. 1513: 'Mansur conquered the [Kara Del] kingdom and brought the region [Hami] under his control in 1513' (Turpan Khanate page), outside the shape (Hami lies east of 92.7E). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1512..1513 from this entry's own 'Valid for 1512-1513 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1512 shape without the Tarim Basin (Altishahr), taken by Said Khan in 1514

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1514-1515: the 1512 shape without the Tarim Basin. Moghulistan page: Sultan Said Khan 'conquered the western Tarim Basin from Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat in 1514' and 'set himself up in Kashgar forming the Yarkent Khanate. Thereafter the Moghulistan khanate was permanently divided.' Cliopatria keeps the Tarim in the Moghulistan row until 1518 and starts Eastern Moghulistan in 1519.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1516 shape without the Tarim Basin (Said Khan's Yarkent Khanate)

keyframe_review.note: 1,365,277 km2 for 1516-1518; the Tarim Basin is removed as in moghulistan_1514. Said Khan page: 'In 1516, he concluded a peace agreement with his older brother Mansur Khan' and 'the eastern part of the settled country south and partly north of Tangri-Tagh joined his state' including Turpan and Kumul: the pages disagree on Turpan (the Turpan Khanate page keeps Mansur there to 1570), so Turfan stays in the shape.

region.text: the western Moghul khanate (Zhetysu, Issyk-Kul and the Fergana edge)

ledger.note: 1463: the Moghul khanate divides and Yunus Khan holds the west. Esen Buqa II 'died of natural causes in 1462, after a khanship of thirty-three years'; 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan.' Cliopatria's western shape begins in 1463; the page does not outline it.

region.text: the settled lands of Eastern Moghulistan (Uyghurstan), the Tarim Basin and Turfan, Dost Muhammad's khanate with its seat at Aksu

ledger.note: 1470: Yunus Khan reunites the khanate. 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate'; Yunus Khan page: Dost died 'in 1468 or 1469, after which Yunus seized Aksu'. The reunion has no date of its own on either page; 1470 is the first year after the death and Cliopatria's shape follows in 1475.

1484: Yunus Khan takes Tashkent. 'In 1484, Yunus Khan took advantage of one of the periodic conflicts' between Sultan Ahmad and Umar Shaikh Mirza II, which allowed him 'to take possession of Tashkent'; the Moghulistan page says both 1482 and 1484.

region.text: Zhetysu and the Issyk-Kul steppe (253,000 km2 by the gazetteer) with Tashkent, the western Moghul line of Mahmud Khan

ledger.note: 1492: Cliopatria splits the Moghul lands. After Yunus's death in 1487 'He was succeeded in Tashkent by his eldest son', Mahmud Khan, 'while the Moghuls in the east followed Ahmad Alaq' (Yunus Khan page); Mahmud is 'the ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent' (Moghulistan page). The year 1492 and the split of Zhetysu into the Eastern Chagatai Khanate row are Cliopatria's; the pages date Ahmad Alaq's Turpan to 1487.

1512: Cliopatria joins the Moghul lands again. The row re-absorbs the Zhetysu of the Eastern Chagatai Khanate (shape ends 1511); the pages do not say so, and the Moghulistan page says the Kyrgyz had 'effectively driven out the Moghuls' by 1510-11. Bridging judgment.

region.text: the western Tarim Basin, Kashgar and the Altishahr cities, from Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat

ledger.note: 1514: Said Khan founds the Yarkent Khanate. Sultan Said Khan 'conquered the western Tarim Basin from Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat in 1514' and 'set himself up in Kashgar forming the Yarkent Khanate'; Said Khan page: expedition against Kashgar from Andijan 'In May 1514', rule of the Yarkent Khanate 'from September 1514'. The page says 'western Tarim Basin' (Altishahr); the whole basin is the researcher's reading.
1518: Cliopatria ends the Moghulistan row; Eastern and Western Moghulistan follow in 1519. The page has the khanate 'permanently divided' by Said Khan's conquest of 1514 and dates no end of its own.

wars.name: Moghul succession war after Esen Buqa II (1462-1469)
wars.outcome: The khanate divided in 1462 between Yunus Khan in the west and Dost Muhammad in the east; Dost died in 1468 or 1469 and Yunus reunited the khanate.
wars.note: The Moghulistan page: 'When Esen Buqa died in 1462, the Dughlat amirs split between his son Dost Muhammad and his brother Yunus Khan.'

wars.name: Yunus Khan's capture of Tashkent (1484)
wars.outcome: Yunus Khan took Tashkent from the Timurids in 1484 during the conflicts between Sultan Ahmad and Umar Shaikh Mirza II; he died there in 1487.
wars.note: The Moghulistan page also says he 'took Tashkent in 1482'.

wars.name: Kyrgyz advance in the Tian Shan (to 1510-1511)
wars.outcome: The Kyrgyz 'gained ground in the Tian Shan' and by 1510-11 had 'effectively driven out the Moghuls'; Cliopatria's Zhetysu stays with the Eastern Chagatai Khanate row to 1511.
wars.note: The page dates only the result ('by 1510-11'); the Kyrgyz 'gained ground' earlier, undated.

wars.name: Mansur Khan's conquest of Hami (1513)
wars.outcome: 'Mansur conquered the kingdom and brought the region under his control in 1513' (Turpan Khanate page); Moghulistan page: Mansur Khan 'captured Hami from Kara Del, a Mongol dependency of Ming China, in 1513'. Hami lies outside Cliopatria's Moghulistan shape.

wars.name: Sultan Said Khan's conquest of Kashgar (1514)
wars.outcome: Said Khan took Kashgar in 1514, 'dethroning Mirza Abu Bakr', and united the Tarim cities into the Yarkent Khanate ('Altishahr'); the Moghulistan khanate was 'permanently divided'.
wars.note: Said Khan page: 'In May 1514, Sultan Said Khan ... made an expedition against Kashgar from Andijan.'

certainty.note: Steppe and oasis frontiers; no page gives a line. Tashkent (1484-1491) and the Tarim oasis cities are points, not borders.

sources.title: Moghulistan

sources.title: Yunus Khan
sources.note: Reign 1462-1487, Aksu, Tashkent 1484, the division between Mahmud and Ahmad Alaq; Dost Muhammad d. 1468 or 1469.

sources.title: Esen Buqa II

sources.title: Sultan Said Khan

sources.title: Turpan Khanate

notes:
Written for batch ia-02-d. Five pages opened (budget 5 for 7 shapes; Esen Buqa II and Yunus Khan are shared with east-turkestan).
Shared Wikidata id Q1191125 (Moghulistan, Eastern Chagatai Khanate, Eastern Moghulistan, Western Moghulistan): these are different Cliopatria rows of one long-lived khanate that Cliopatria cuts into halves. The pieces do not overlap: Moghulistan 1463-1474 is the west (Yunus), East Turkestan 1463-1474 the east (Dost Muhammad), Moghulistan 1475-1491 both together, Moghulistan 1492-1511 the Tarim and Turfan with Eastern Chagatai Khanate 1492-1511 the Zhetysu (= the Cliopatria Moghulistan 1491 shape minus its 1492 shape, exactly), Moghulistan 1512-1518 both again; from 1519 Eastern Moghulistan (Tarim) and Western Moghulistan (Zhetysu). I kept the row as its own dossier (the first row of Q1191125 in time, which this batch owns) and did not merge the others: eastern-chagatai-khanate (ia-02) and the 1519 rows (ia-03) have their own owners; the orchestrator may merge them if it prefers one state.
Settled: the 1462/63 division, the 1469/70 reunion, Tashkent 1484, the 1514 Yarkent Khanate.
Corrected: moghulistan_1468, _1482, _1512 (years only, valid for 1468-1469, 1482-1483, 1512-1513), new keyframes 1470 (reunion), 1484 (Tashkent added), 1514 (Tarim Basin removed); moghulistan_1516 (Tarim removed). The Tarim removal leaves Tarim without a Cliopatria owner in 1514-1518 until Eastern Moghulistan begins in 1519 (938,000 km2): the eastern-moghulistan dossier should start with Said Khan in 1514.
Unsettled: Tashkent 1482 or 1484 (Moghulistan page gives both); the 1492 split and the 1512 reunion are Cliopatria's years (confidence 1); Kyrgyz 'driven out the Moghuls' by 1510-11 against Cliopatria's Zhetysu in the 1512 shape; Turpan and Kumul after 1516 (Said Khan page: joined his state; Turpan Khanate page: Mansur kept Turpan to 1570); the Dughlat amirs' nominal vassalage (Mirza Abu Bakr held Kashgar, Yarkand and Khotan, undated) is not recorded; Mahmud Khan's fall to Shaybani (reign 'to 1508', no year of the defeat on the page); no seat for 1463-1469.
Needs a dossier from another group: turpan-khanate (Turpan Khanate, 1487 to 1570 or later, Cliopatria lacks it; suggested group ia-02-x or ia-03); the Dughlat emirate of Kashgar (Mirza Abu Bakr, 1465-1514 on the Yunus/Moghulistan pages) and Kara Del (Hami) are also not drawn.
Not opened (budget): Mahmud Khan, Mansur Khan, Ahmad Alaq, Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat, Dughlat, Yarkent Khanate, Kara Del, Kyrgyz people.
Gazetteer: 'Moghulistan' is no region (Zhetysu, Issyk-Kul, Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami are used instead).
